title: Unbounded pro-etale direct image commutes with open restriction
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $p:V\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and set $U=V\times_TW$, with projections $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $r:U\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the uncompleted unbounded derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For every $L\in D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the canonical restriction map
$$\rho_L:i^*Rp_*L\longrightarrow Rr_*k^*L$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $L$. Its normalization is the termwise equality $i^*p_*I=r_*k^*I$ on a K-injective representative $I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]; on $Q\to W$ both sides evaluate on $V\times_TQ=U\times_WQ$, with the same restrictions and $A$-actions. Open restriction $k^*$ preserves K-injectives, using $k_!\dashv k^*$ [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and exact $k_!$ [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. With exact extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and its open unit [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit], this gives the natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_M:i^*Rp_*k_!M\xrightarrow{\rho}Rr_*k^*k_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_*M$$
for every $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. No properness, cohomological-dimension bound, boundedness or etale-origin hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], the projection $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ is an open immersion. For a module sheaf $F$ on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, identify open inverse image with restriction using [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (including the identifications of constant ring sheaves). For every object $Q\to W$, the direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives
$$(i^*p_*F)(Q)=F(V\times_TQ),\qquad(r_*k^*F)(Q)=F(U\times_WQ).$$
The Cartesian identity $U=V\times_TW$ [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies these objects over $V$. A morphism $Q'\to Q$ induces the same morphism between their fibre products, so the identifications commute with restrictions and with maps of $F$. Both module actions come from the same map $Q\to T$ on constant ring sheaves, hence this is an $A_W$-linear natural isomorphism $\alpha_F:i^*p_*F\simeq r_*k^*F$. This is the open-restriction map: its component sends a section on $V\times_TQ$ to that same section on $U\times_WQ$. Applying it in every degree commutes with differentials and gives $\alpha_I$ for any complex $I$.

source.place: lemma-morphism-big-small, pushforward formula; elementary Cartesian calculation; localization as in Definition 09AE (definition-extension-zero); schemes.tex Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), open-immersion case

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] to $k:U\hookrightarrow V$: $k_!\dashv k^*$. The coefficient ring is finite commutative, and $k$ is an open immersion, so [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] makes $k_!$ exact. Both functors are additive between the abelian module-sheaf categories. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], with $u=k^*$ and $v=k_!$, shows that $k^*I$ is K-injective whenever $I$ is. These are exactly its hypotheses; neither properness nor a bound on the degrees of $I$ is used.

Represent $L$ by a complex $C$ and choose $C\to I$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Its small-site hypothesis holds by the skeleton/universe convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and its ring is $A_V$. In the uncompleted operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], $Rp_*L$ is represented by $p_*I$. Exactness of $i^*$ and $k^*$ gives representatives $i^*p_*I$ for $i^*Rp_*L$ and $k^*I$ for $k^*L$. Step 2 says $k^*I$ is K-injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] it therefore computes $Rr_*k^*L$ as $r_*k^*I$, whether or not it is the chosen functorial resolution. Here the functor on the homotopy category is the termwise additive $r_*$ followed by localization; it preserves shifts and cone triangles since these use finite direct sums. The comparison is consequently represented by $\alpha_I$ from step 1, a degreewise isomorphism of complexes. This proves that $\rho_L$ is an isomorphism with the stated normalization.

To check naturality and independence, represent two objects by K-injective complexes $I,J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], each derived morphism between them is represented by a chain map $h:I\to J$, unique up to homotopy. The square formed by $i^*p_*h$, $r_*k^*h$, $\alpha_I$, and $\alpha_J$ commutes: on $Q\to W$ both paths are the map of sections induced by $h$ on the same fibre product, in every degree. Additive termwise functors take a chain homotopy to a chain homotopy by applying the functor to $h^n$ in the identity $f-g=dh+hd$, so the square depends only on the derived morphism. The same cited lemma makes a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives a homotopy equivalence; applying these functors preserves its inverse and homotopies. Changing the K-injective representative therefore gives the same transformation under the derived comparison identifications. Thus $\rho$ is natural on the entire unbounded derived category.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), equivalence with maps in the derived category; elementary sectionwise naturality

proof.text:
Finally [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] makes the termwise $k_!$ a functor on the derived category: an exact additive functor preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology, hence sends acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms to such complexes and maps. Exactness of $k^*$ is part of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The natural open unit of [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit] is an isomorphism in each degree of every complex representing $M$, and commutes with differentials by naturality. It induces $\eta_M:M\xrightarrow{\sim}k^*k_!M$. Apply step 3 to $L=k_!M$ and then apply $Rr_*$ to $\eta_M^{-1}$. Their composite
$$i^*Rp_*k_!M\xrightarrow{\rho_{k_!M}}Rr_*k^*k_!M\xrightarrow{Rr_*(\eta_M^{-1})}Rr_*M$$
is precisely $\lambda_M$ and is a natural isomorphism. No claim that $k_!$ preserves K-injectives is used: step 3 resolves $k_!M$ on $V$. All arguments apply for arbitrary opens and arbitrary unbounded complexes.
